task.title: Tighten tests and rough edges left by the tasks-remote review
task.description:
Follow-ups from the third review of PR #219 (Share tasks through a remote other than origin). None loses data.

Tests that do not bite:
- The tasks-only repoint test uses an empty repository as its wrong address, which a later check refuses anyway. Use a non-empty copy of the same project so removing the marker-address check fails the test.
- Credential stripping in the publication-unconfirmed warning has no assertion.
- The content check in the move's carry step is untested (verification catches the same forgery afterwards).
- The hand-off check on the CLI path is redundant with the listing made when the command opens the project; remove it or test it.

Rough edges:
- After two moves, a stale first-generation checkout or tasks-only folder is pointed at the intermediate place and needs a second setup to reach the final one.
- A leftover probe ref whose name sorts after the current run's (a machine with a fast clock) is never removed.
- Operations summarized by a compaction checkpoint are matched by ID only, and the compacted replay paths in sync skip the content check; the reference says 'by ID and by content'.
- After an interrupted repoint, the finishing run omits movedFrom.
- With a set-aside edit, move-tasks still reports verified:true and 'holding every operation'.
- A board that shares a repository handle with its loop can, in a narrow race, show a loop round's publication-unconfirmed warning on an unrelated inline save.
